info.title: ant0d (CLI subset)
info.description: Subset of the Ant0 desktop local API used by this CLI.

get.description: Open (no bearer token). Clients use it to find a running daemon.

With `integrity=true` every item also carries `integrity`: whether its files still match the release's signed file proof (`ok`, `failed` with the changed file, or `unchecked`). This is a corruption check for display only, not an anti-tamper control, and launch does not depend on it (the SDK's launch check looks only at file names and sizes). Reinstall a `failed` release. With `capabilities=true` every item also carries `capabilities` (what the release can do for a profile's settings, e.g. `canvas_noise`).

parameters.name: capabilities
parameters.description: Add `capabilities` to every item: what the release can do for a profile's settings (`canvas_noise`). Off by default so the plain list keeps the fields older readers expect.

parameters.name: integrity
parameters.description: Check each installed release against its signed file proof and add `integrity` to every item. Reads the whole engine once, so the first answer can take a few seconds; unchanged files are not read again.

put.description: The release profiles without a pinned `browser.version` launch. Must be installed (404 `browser.not_found`). Answers the updated list.

get.summary: Look up an available browser release
get.description: Contacts the release store (the only outbound host besides proxies). An explicit version reads its immutable manifest without following the channel pointer.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Exact immutable release version; omitted = resolve the channel.

size_bytes.description: Download size of this platform's archive; null only when a channel's manifest is unavailable. Exact-version lookup fails instead.

post.description: Answers 202 immediately. Progress streams as `browser.install` events; poll `GET /v1/browsers/jobs/{id}` for the outcome. Installing an already installed version completes at once. A fresh install is built in a staging directory and committed only after its signed file proof verified: a proof that is invalid or files that do not match it fail the job (`proof_invalid` / `proof_mismatch`) and leave nothing behind; a proof the store does not have or cannot deliver is recorded and the install succeeds. With `repair_proof` an installed release gains its signed `.provenance` without reinstalling. With `replace` an installed release is installed again in staging and swapped in only after it verified (see the body).

version.description: Pin a release; omitted = the channel's current version.

replace.description: Reinstall an already installed release: needs an exact `version`. The release is downloaded and verified again in a staging directory (signed file proof included) and swapped in atomically only when everything passed, so a failure leaves the installed release as it was. The default release, pins and profile references are not touched. 404 `browser.not_found` when it is not installed; 409 `browser.in_use` while a running profile uses it or another install runs. Absent or false keeps the normal install.

repair_proof.description: Repair the signed file proof (`.provenance`) of an already installed release instead of installing: needs an exact `version`, fetches only the public proof and release metadata, checks the installed files against the signed inventory and writes the proof only on a complete match. Repair may set file modes to the signed inventory's modes after content matches; it never changes file contents. Never downloads the engine or reinstalls. Absent or false keeps the normal install.

delete.description: 409 `browser.in_use` while a running profile uses it; 409 `browser.is_default` when it is the default and nothing else is installed (otherwise the newest remaining release becomes the default).

post.description: Ids (UUID or exact name, at most 50) are processed one after another; a failing id is reported with its error code and the rest proceed. 400 when there are more than 50. `patch.group` replaces (null clears the label), `tags_add` then `tags_remove` edit the tags, `pinned` and `status` replace, `proxy_id` (null = direct) and `webrtc` set the network fields. Each item is the same edit as `PATCH /v1/profiles/:id` with the equivalent body, with the same checks (an unknown `proxy_id` fails that item with 404 `proxy.not_found`); a running profile keeps its current settings until its next start. Trashed profiles are updated too. UUID/name aliases are deduplicated, then each unique profile is authorized and edited sequentially. Authorization and edit errors retain the input reference in `errors`; other items proceed. Earlier edits remain committed when a later item fails. Successful bindings are rechecked before delivering the overall result. Sync-mapped profiles require fresh cloud owner/manager/operator membership and exact remote-profile/folder visibility before any edit. Starter or missing permission returns 403 `team.forbidden`; offline, malformed or incomplete evidence fails closed (503), and cloud rate limits return 429. Authorization has a ten-second/100-page aggregate budget, with no cached-role or offline-grace fallback. Session/workspace or mapping changes return 409 `licence.session_changed` / `sync.conflict`. Existing mutation locks apply: 409 `sync.locked` / `sync.transfer_conflict`, 423 `sync.locked` for a locked vault. Unmapped profiles need no cloud calls, but missing authorization infrastructure returns 503 `sync.store_unavailable` even for local edits. `group` is a local label, not a cloud folder move or grant. A late binding change suppresses success without rolling back committed edits; do not automatically retry an ambiguous mutation.

patch.description: `group` replaces (null clears); `tags_add` then `tags_remove` edit the tag list; `pinned` and `status` replace (null clears the status); `proxy_id` sets `network.proxy_id` (null = direct connection) and `webrtc` sets `network.webrtc`, exactly as `PATCH /v1/profiles/:id` would.

get.description: `id` is the profile UUID or its exact name. `runtime` is the live session or null; `deleted_at` is set while in the trash; `platform` as in the list summaries. Non-null sessions require fresh cloud owner/manager/operator membership and exact mapped remote-profile/folder visibility. Starter or missing permission returns 403 `team.forbidden`; offline, malformed or incomplete evidence fails closed (503), and rate limits return 429. Authorization has a ten-second/100-page per-profile budget, without cached-role or offline-grace fallback. Session/workspace or mapping changes return 409 `licence.session_changed` / `sync.conflict`; browser replacement or changed launch/endpoint fields return 409 `sync.conflict`. Missing authorization infrastructure returns 503 `sync.store_unavailable` even for empty/stopped reads, before profile resolution. Stopped profiles and unmapped sessions need no cloud calls. These reads connect to no CDP socket and perform no browser or profile mutation.

delete.summary: Move a profile to the trash (or delete it for good)
delete.description: `id` is the profile UUID or its exact name. Moves the profile to the trash, where it stays restorable for `trash_retention_days` (30) before the sweeper purges it. `?permanent=true` deletes the row, launch history and user data immediately (and releases the cloud claim; the trash keeps it). 409 `profile.running` while it runs. A Cloud profile answers 409 `profile.synced` unless `?cloud=trash` also moves its cloud copy to the cloud Trash (409 `sync.lease_held`, `sync.conflict`; 503 `sync.store_unavailable` offline).

parameters.name: permanent
parameters.description: Skip the trash: delete the row, launch history and user data for good. Default: move to the trash (30-day retention).

parameters.name: purge
parameters.description: Deprecated alias of `permanent` (the older name).

parameters.name: cloud
parameters.description: For a Cloud profile: also move its cloud copy to the cloud Trash, then this profile to the local trash. Without it a Cloud profile answers 409 `profile.synced`. Not allowed with `permanent`.

post.description: `id` is the profile UUID or its exact name. Resolves when the DevTools endpoint is up. 409 `profile.already_running`. Independent API keys require profiles:run and profiles:cdp with fresh signed authority; interactive requests require CDP disclosure authorization before launch and again before returning the full Session: mapped profiles need fresh owner/manager/operator membership and exact remote-profile/folder visibility. Starter or missing permission returns 403 `team.forbidden`; offline, malformed or incomplete evidence fails closed (503), and rate limits return 429. Each permission pass has its own ten-second/100-page budget including token retries, without cached-role or offline-grace fallback; the entire launch is not limited to ten seconds. Unmapped profiles need no cloud calls but retain binding fences. Missing authorization infrastructure returns 503 `sync.store_unavailable` before resolution, even for unmapped or unknown profiles. Session/workspace changes return 409 `licence.session_changed`; mapping changes, redirected launches or browser/session changes return generic 409 `sync.conflict`. Existing launcher licence/lease/checkpoint and error handling applies, including 423 `profile.locked`. Late denial or a lost response may leave a browser running; there is no automatic stop or rollback. Do not automatically retry an ambiguous start: inspect lifecycle state and guarded runtime GETs when permitted first.

Sync-mapped profiles require the same fresh cloud membership (owner, manager or operator) and folder-scoped visibility as cookie export, before CDP access, pending-cookie changes or dirty-state bookkeeping. There is no cached-role or offline-grace fallback. Session/workspace, mapping or browser-session changes and conflicting sync operations reject the mutation (409); a locked sync vault returns 423 `sync.locked`. A change detected after browser dispatch cannot undo the command; do not automatically retry an ambiguous mutation. Unmapped local profiles retain their existing cookie behavior. Pending imports are authorized when queued, not reauthorized when applied at launch.

get.description: Full proxy documents can contain provider credentials in change_ip_url; passwords remain opaque password_ref values. Every current referencing profile (including trash) is authorized in one batch. Sync-mapped references require fresh owner/manager/operator membership and exact remote-profile/folder visibility, with one thirty-second/1,000-page visibility listing per request and no cached-role or offline fallback. Denial returns 403 `team.forbidden`; rate limits return 429; unavailable, malformed or incomplete evidence fails closed (503). Authorization infrastructure is required even for empty inventories and unused proxies (503 `sync.store_unavailable`); unused/unmapped references need no cloud calls. Exact reference sets and all captured binding fences are checked before delivery; changes return 409 `sync.conflict` / `licence.session_changed`. Current documents are read synchronously after preflight and fences. Reads do not decrypt passwords, probe/rotate proxies, acquire configuration-mutation locks, dirty profiles, clean transfers or emit mutation events. Authorization covers current manifest references, not historical running-session dependencies; these request-time checks are not an atomic cloud lease or instantaneous revocation. The IDs matching q/tag are snapshotted and every selected proxy is authorized in one batch. The final filtered ID set must match exactly, and all earlier reference/binding fences are rechecked: changed selection returns 409 `sync.conflict`; deletion during preflight may return 404 `proxy.not_found`. No partial success or newly matching unauthorized objects are returned. Current fields and sort order may change if selection and bindings still match.

Single forms answer the created proxy; `{ lines }` answers `{ created, errors }` with 1-based line numbers for rows that failed.

post.description: TCP reachability followed by exit-IP/geo lookup; SOCKS5 and SOCKS4 use a temporary loopback relay (SOCKS4 as SOCKS4a, host names unresolved), closed afterwards. Bad proxies return `ok: false` with a safe diagnostic stored as `last_check`; authorization failures remain HTTP errors. Every current referencing profile (including trash) is authorized in one batch. Sync-mapped references require fresh owner/manager/operator membership and exact remote-profile/folder visibility, with one thirty-second/1,000-page visibility listing per request and no cached-role or offline fallback. Denial returns 403 `team.forbidden`; rate limits return 429; unavailable, malformed or incomplete evidence fails closed (503). Infrastructure is required even for unused proxies (503 `sync.store_unavailable`); unused/unmapped references need no cloud calls. Exact usage and all binding fences are checked before probing, between asynchronous stages and before recording/delivery. Changed bindings or connection configuration return 409 `sync.conflict` / `licence.session_changed`; deletion returns 404. Unrelated current fields are preserved; unchanged concurrent checks record in completion order, with start timestamps. Checks perform no configuration edits, dirty bookkeeping or transfer cleanup and acquire no configuration-mutation locks. Authorization covers current manifest references, not historical running-session dependencies. A pre-record conflict preserves prior diagnostics; a final conflict can suppress delivery after recording. Dispatched traffic cannot be recalled; do not automatically retry ambiguity or assume instantaneous cloud revocation.

post.description: GETs the provider's `change_ip_url` and reports the HTTP status. 400 `validation_failed` when the proxy has no `change_ip_url`; 400 `proxy.change_ip_refused` when the URL is disallowed by the SSRF guard (non-http(s) scheme, credentials in the URL, or a host that resolves to a loopback/link-local/metadata/multicast address — or a private LAN address unless the proxy's own host is itself on the LAN — including redirect hops); 502 `proxy.change_ip_failed` when the request itself fails. The refusal reveals nothing about whether an internal host answered. Every current referencing profile (including trash) is authorized in one batch. Sync-mapped references require fresh owner/manager/operator membership and exact remote-profile/folder visibility, with one thirty-second/1,000-page visibility listing per request and no cached-role or offline-grace fallback. Denial returns 403 `team.forbidden`; cloud rate limits return 429; offline, malformed or incomplete evidence fails closed (503). Authorization infrastructure is required even for unused proxies (503 `sync.store_unavailable`); unused proxies and unmapped references need no cloud calls. Exact usage and all binding fences are checked immediately before dispatch and after awaiting the result; changes return 409 `sync.conflict` / `licence.session_changed`. The current URL is read after preflight. The provider request keeps its ten-second timeout; redirects are followed manually (at most three hops, each re-validated by the same SSRF rules), and the connection is pinned to the validated address so a DNS rebind cannot switch the target. Rotation performs no local configuration mutation, dirty bookkeeping or transfer cleanup and acquires no configuration-mutation locks. Authorization covers current manifest references, not historical proxy dependencies of already-running sessions; browsers are not restarted or reconfigured. After dispatch, a timeout, transport error or final conflict can suppress success even though the IP was rotated. That external effect cannot be undone; do not automatically retry an ambiguous result. These checks are not an atomic cloud/provider lease or instantaneous revocation.

delete.summary: Remove an extension from the library
delete.description: 409 `extension.in_use` (`details.profile_ids`) while profiles reference it; `?force=true` authorizes every referencing profile (including trash) sequentially before removing paths, then reports edits in `updated_profiles`. Sync-mapped profiles require fresh owner/manager/operator membership and exact remote-profile/folder visibility, with a ten-second/100-page budget per profile and no cached-role or offline-grace fallback. Permission denial returns 403 `team.forbidden`; cloud rate limits return 429; offline, malformed or incomplete evidence fails closed (503). Unmapped profiles need no cloud calls. Forced deletion requires authorization infrastructure even without references (503 `sync.store_unavailable`). Usage or binding changes return 409 `sync.conflict` / `licence.session_changed`. Existing mutation locks apply: 409 `sync.locked` / `sync.transfer_conflict`, or 423 `sync.locked` for a locked vault. A pre-deletion failure retains library files but may leave earlier profile edits committed. Filesystem deletion is not transactional. A final binding conflict suppresses success without rolling back edits/deletion; do not automatically retry an ambiguous removal.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Also remove the path from every profile's `launch.extensions` instead of answering 409 `extension.in_use`.

get.description: `state`: `signed_out`, `active`, `grace` (offline past `expires_at`, before `grace_until`: existing profiles start, nothing is created), `locked` (past grace, no token, or the workspace lapsed), `suspended`. `used` counts live and trashed profiles. `keep` lists the profiles that stay startable while `used` exceeds `limits.profiles`. `mode: off` means nothing is enforced (development).

200.description: What the daemon knows about its licence: the response of GET /v1/licence and of every licence mutation. Never carries tokens.

post.summary: Ask the cloud for a fresh licence now
post.description: Runs the hourly `POST /licence` immediately and answers the resulting state (200 even when the cloud is unreachable: `online: false`, `last_error`, and the stored token keeps applying until `grace_until`).

post.summary: Sign in to the Ant0 cloud (CLI users)
post.description: Forwards the credentials to `api.ant0.link`, registers this device and fetches the first licence. Cloud errors keep their code and status: 401 `auth.invalid_credentials`, 401 `auth.totp_required` (retry with `totp`), 401 `auth.totp_invalid`, 403 `device.limit`, 409 `device.free_used`, 429 `auth.rate_limited`; 503 `licence.offline` when the cloud does not answer. The desktop app signs in itself and uses `POST /v1/licence/session`.

schema.description: Credentials are forwarded to the cloud once and never stored; the daemon keeps the resulting refresh token.

totp.description: 6-digit TOTP code or a recovery code, when 2FA is enabled.

requestBody.description: Credentials are forwarded to the cloud once and never stored; the daemon keeps the resulting refresh token.

200.description: What the daemon knows about its licence: the response of GET /v1/licence and of every licence mutation. Never carries tokens.

post.description: Revokes the cloud session (best effort) and forgets the session and licence token; the state becomes `signed_out`. The keep list is kept locally.

get.description: A plain GET returns `{ items: Ant0Event[] }`. Without a WebSocket subprotocol the stream continues to send raw event-v1 JSON (default replay 50; `since` and `limit` supported). Offer only `ant0-events.v1` for opt-in ant0-events/v1 replay.begin, event, replay.end frames (default replay 200, max 200); `after=generation:seq` is an exclusive cursor valid only on framed WebSockets. The server echoes the negotiated subprotocol. `?token=` may replace the Authorization header for WebSocket clients. HTTP history and every WebSocket mode redact `profile.state` to type/profile_id/state/at and optional pid/exit_code; no `cdp_url` or endpoint. Use authorized detail/status GETs for endpoints.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Raw/HTTP only: replay buffered events at or after this time.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Framed WebSocket only: exclusive generation:sequence cursor; a cursor is not authorization.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Bearer token for WebSocket clients that cannot set headers.

details.description: Ajv issues for validation_failed; `{ code, path }` for storage.*; `{ code }` (the daemon-side install code) for browser.* install failures.

Session.title: Ant0 session v1
Session.description: A running browser session: the response of POST /v1/profiles/:id/start and the element of GET /v1/sessions.

cdp_http.description: HTTP base of the DevTools endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:9333.

Proxy.title: Ant0 proxy v1
Proxy.description: Stored proxy document (schema "ant0-proxy/v1"). Passwords are never stored inline; password_ref points at the secrets table.

host.description: Hostname, IPv4, or bare IPv6 address (no brackets).

change_ip_url.description: Provider "change IP" link, fetched with GET on demand.

session_pattern.description: e.g. "user-{session}" substituted into the username per launch.

udp.description: socks5 only: pass --socks5-udp so WebRTC/QUIC traverse the proxy. Ignored for http/https/socks4 (not enforced by this schema). Default false.
socks5 with udp set: one STUN request through the proxy's UDP. Absent when not tried.

same_ip.description: Whether the UDP address equals the exit IP; null when either is unknown.

dns_ok.description: Whether a name lookup with the chosen DNS-over-HTTPS service worked, through the proxy.

reason.description: refused | auth | unreachable | timeout | no_reply | error; null when ok.

Cookie.title: Ant0 cookie v1
Cookie.description: Normalized Playwright cookie shape. Cookie-Editor/EditThisCookie JSON, Puppeteer/Playwright arrays and Netscape cookies.txt are converted to this.

domain.description: Leading dot = also sent to subdomains; no dot = host-only.

expires.description: Unix time in seconds; -1 for a session cookie.

Ant0Event.title: Ant0 event v1
Ant0Event.description: One event on the WebSocket /v1/events stream (JSON lines). Discriminated on "type".

Ant0EventProfileLifecycle.description: Trash lifecycle: moved to the trash, restored from it, or purged (row and directory gone).

Ant0EventInventoryBulkChanged.description: One coalesced notice for a bulk request (trash, restore, purge, adopt, proxy delete): refetch the listed inventory kinds instead of tracking per-item events.

code.description: With phase `error`: the daemon-side failure code (`download_interrupted`, `checksum_mismatch`, `store_unreachable`, `disk_full`, `release_signature`, `release_error`, `install_failed`, …).

auto.description: Set on every event of an automatic engine update (the daemon's own, not a user request).

Ant0EventLicenceChanged.description: The licence state changed: sign-in/out, a refresh, a plan change, entering offline grace, lock or suspension. Read GET /v1/licence for the full picture.

LicenceState.title: Ant0 licence state v1
LicenceState.description: What the daemon knows about its licence: the response of GET /v1/licence and of every licence mutation. Never carries tokens.

state.description: signed_out: no cloud session; active: token valid (now <= exp); grace: offline grace (exp < now <= grace); locked: past grace, no token, or the server refused (lapsed); suspended: the server answered workspace.suspended.

mode.description: enforce: the licence rules apply; off: development mode (ANT0_LICENCE_MODE=off), nothing is enforced and launches carry no ticket unless a licence is present anyway.

plan.description: Plan id from the token (free, p10, p50, p200, p1000); null without a token.

used.description: Profiles counted against the plan: the larger of `used_local` and the workspace-wide active claim count the cloud last reported (claims made on other devices included). Shown to the user; the local gates use `used_local`.

used_local.description: Profiles holding a claim on this device: live plus trashed rows (the trash keeps its claim so restores are free; purge releases it). Drives the keep list and the over-the-limit lock.

features.description: Feature flags from the token (`feat`), e.g. api, sync, teams, mcp, priority_support.

billing.description: Subscription status from the token (`st`); informational, enforcement follows `limits`.

device_id.description: base32(SHA-256(hw)[0..16]), 26 characters; null when the hardware fingerprint could not be computed.

sign_pub.description: This daemon's device signing public key (Ed25519, 32 raw bytes, standard base64) — the `sign_pub` it registers and the `dpk` a licence should name. The desktop shell compares it with its own and hands its keys over when they differ. Public material; null before the keys are loaded.

account_id.description: The signed-in account (user id) of this daemon's session; null when signed out or not yet known. The desktop shell requires it to equal its own account before it treats the daemon as ready. Absent on older daemons; treat absence as unknown.

online.description: True when the last POST /v1/licence to the cloud succeeded.

checked.description: False while the start-up refresh of this daemon process is still in flight: `state` then reflects the cached token judged against the clock (it may read grace or locked after a long closure) and is not yet confirmed by the cloud. True once that refresh has an outcome (success or failure) or when there was nothing to refresh. Absent on older daemons; treat absence as true.

capabilities.description: Optional protocol features this daemon understands. `registered_kx_marker`: the daemon checks the registered-key marker (`device_keys.registered_kx_fingerprint`) on a key hand-over, so the desktop app may send it. Absent on older daemons; treat absence as none.

logout_seq.description: Count of explicit sign-outs of this daemon (`POST /v1/licence/sign-out`), persisted and never decreased by the daemon. Hand-overs, adoptions, lost or expired sessions and refresh failures do not change it. The desktop app compares it with the value it last accepted to tell a command-line logout from a lost session. Absent on older daemons.

last_error.description: Why the last refresh failed (a cloud error code or `network`); null after a success.

keep.description: Profiles allowed to start while `used` exceeds `limits.profiles` ("lapsed to Free"). `explicit` is true once the user chose (POST /v1/licence/keep); otherwise the daemon's default pick is shown. Empty when the limit is not exceeded.

message.description: One human sentence for the current state ("Reconnect within 47 h", "Plan allows 5 profiles"), or null when nothing needs attention.

ProxyCreate.description: Proxy in object form. `password` is plaintext on input only; responses carry `password_ref`.

ProfileManifest.title: Ant0 profile manifest v1
ProfileManifest.description: Canonical stored profile document (schema "ant0-profile/v1"). Runtime state (running, pid, cdp url) is not part of the manifest.

pinned.description: Pinned rows sort first in clients. Default false.

version.description: Pinned release, e.g. "149.0.7827.114-ant0.1"; null = newest installed.

key.description: synthetic: deterministic identity key; defaults to the profile id.

profile_ref.description: captured: file under identities/, relative (no absolute paths, no parent traversal).

canvas.description: Canvas/WebGL readback: "real" = this computer's genuine output (default), "noise" = per-profile noise. Absent = noise when overrides.canvasNoise or overrides.fingerprintNoise is true, else real.

display_max.description: Deprecated and ignored. Written by desktop 0.3.21-beta.6 ("Match my display"); tolerated on read, dropped on the next write, never sent to the cloud.

display_match.description: Deprecated and ignored. Written by desktop 0.3.21-beta.6 ("Match my display"); tolerated on read, dropped on the next write, never sent to the cloud.

source.description: proxy: derive timezone/languages/location from the exit IP at launch.

ProfileOverrides.description: Allowlisted subset of the Node SDK IdentityOverrides.

extensions.description: Absolute paths to unpacked extensions (POSIX "/..." or Windows "X:\...").

extra_args.description: Power users; identity switches are rejected by the SDK.

ProfileDetail.title: Ant0 profile detail
ProfileDetail.description: profile-manifest-v1 plus `runtime` (the live session, or null when stopped), `deleted_at` (RFC 3339 while in the trash, else null) and `platform` (the OS persona the browser presents, as in ProfileSummary).

pinned.description: Pinned rows sort first in clients. Default false.

platform.description: OS persona the browser presents: `overrides.platform` (passed to the engine as `--fingerprint-platform`), else the OS of the persisted synthetic/captured persona (`compatibility.os_family`, known once the identity has been previewed or launched); null when neither is known or the identity is native.

ProfileInput.title: Ant0 profile input
ProfileInput.description: Partial profile-manifest-v1 for PATCH: objects merge, arrays and scalars replace. `network.proxy` may carry an inline proxy instead of `proxy_id`; `overrides.<key>: null` removes that override.

version.description: Pinned release, e.g. "149.0.7827.114-ant0.1"; null = newest installed.

key.description: synthetic: deterministic identity key; defaults to the profile id.

ProfileInputOverrides.description: Allowlisted subset of the Node SDK IdentityOverrides. On input every key also accepts null: the override is removed from the manifest (PATCH) or left unset (create).

ProfileCreate.title: Ant0 profile create
ProfileCreate.description: Profile create request: `name` is required, everything else defaults.

pinned.description: Pinned rows sort first in clients. Default false.

model_version.description: Create-only: the identity model version asked of the cloud for this profile's fresh persona (hints.model_version). Absent = the default. Not stored in the manifest.

status.description: ok: every file matches the signed inventory. failed: a file was changed, removed or added, or the proof itself no longer verifies; reinstall the release. unchecked: there is no signed proof on disk to check against, or the check did not finish.

path.description: With `failed`: the changed file, relative to the release's `browser/`.

canvas_noise.description: Whether this release supports per-profile canvas Noise (158.0.8127.18-ant0.9 and later). On earlier releases Noise shows the computer's real output.

reinstall.description: Whether this daemon can reinstall an installed release in place (`replace` on `POST /v1/browsers/install`). Always true here; an older daemon has no `capabilities` at all.

default.description: True for exactly one installed release: the one unpinned profiles launch (PUT /v1/browsers/default; newest installed when unset).

status.description: verified: signed proof checked and present. missing: the store has no proof for this release. unavailable: the proof could not be fetched or written. invalid: a signature or schema check failed. mismatch: the installed files differ from the signed inventory.

changed.description: Whether `.provenance` was created or replaced (verified only).

version.description: Known once the channel resolved (immediately when pinned).

phase.description: Latest progress phase; null before the download starts.

bytes.description: Progress in the phase's unit (bytes for download/verify, entries for extract).

total.description: Total in the same unit; 0 when unknown (no Content-Length).

engine_proof.description: Outcome of the signed file proof step (`.provenance`); null until known. A finished install can be done with a status other than `verified`.

platform.description: OS persona the browser presents: `overrides.platform` (passed to the engine as `--fingerprint-platform`), else the OS of the persisted synthetic/captured persona (`compatibility.os_family`, known once the identity has been previewed or launched); null when neither is known or the identity is native.

deleted_at.description: Set while the profile is in the trash (`GET /v1/profiles?trashed=true`).

platform.description: OS persona the browser presents: `overrides.platform` (passed to the engine as `--fingerprint-platform`), else the OS of the persisted synthetic/captured persona (`compatibility.os_family`, known once the identity has been previewed or launched); null when neither is known or the identity is native.

purge_at.description: When the sweeper will purge it: `deleted_at` + `trash_retention_days`.

from_cloud.description: Present when the profile was a Cloud profile moved to Trash together with its cloud copy (`?cloud=trash`). Restoring it brings it back on this computer only.

id.description: Library id: the Web Store id when the manifest has a `key`, else `<slug>-<8 hex>`.

icon_path.description: Absolute path of the largest manifest icon, or null.

icon_data_url.description: The icon as a base64 `data:` URL when it is at most 64 KB; else null.

path.description: Absolute library folder; this is what `launch.extensions` holds.
